correctness.rationale: The proper NC7 order complex of rank-six lattice has 427 vertices and is simply connected by the primary EL-shellability result. The D7 action is without simplex inversions since chain ranks are preserved, and every reflection has a fixed nontrivial partition vertex; Armstrong gives simply connected quotient. A NEW independently written exhaustive restricted-growth partition and dihedral orbit-chain enumeration recovered original chain counts (427,6468,25382,36015,16807), quotient cells (47,542,1954,2680,1231), and signed boundary nonzeros (0,1084,5862,10720,6155). Independently implemented integer unit-chain cancellations took 3221 pivots to residual groups (1,0,0,1,10), with ten degree-four coefficients (14,7,7,-14,14,7,-14,14,-14,14), gcd=7. Hence H3=Z/7,H4=Z^9 and no other reduced integral groups. A simply-connected 4-CW complex with H2=0 is 2-connected, its 3-skeleton a wedge S3 and degree classification gives M(Z/7,3) wedge nine S4. The exact computation is finite, not an all-size classification.

value.rationale: A natural dihedral quotient of the classical seven-point noncrossing-partition lattice acquires 7-primary torsion not present in the torsion-free covering sphere wedge. The full integral homotopy type including a Moore space and nine free spheres is a meaningful exact symmetry-topology invariant, providing an explicit case that rational orbit counts cannot detect.

limitations: The quotient classification relies on standard Armstrong orbit-space hypotheses and the Hurewicz/Whitehead CW homotopy reduction, rather than a formal proof assistant.
Unindexed computations of seven-point dihedral NC quotient might predate this result; all-size classifications are not asserted.
